note: Curated local subset of MITRE ATT&CK for Enterprise used by ACR. Stored locally so the engine never depends on an external API.

techniques.name: Phishing
techniques.description: Adversary may send phishing messages to gain access to victim systems.
techniques.detection_hint: Mail client spawned unusual children; user clicked attachment/link.

techniques.name: Phishing: Spearphishing Attachment
techniques.description: Malicious attachment delivered via targeted email.
techniques.detection_hint: Office application launched from mail client and spawned a shell.

techniques.name: Phishing: Spearphishing Link
techniques.description: Malicious link delivered via targeted email.
techniques.detection_hint: Browser opened shortly after mail delivery with crafted URL.

techniques.name: Valid Accounts
techniques.description: Adversary may use valid credentials to maintain access to systems.
techniques.detection_hint: Successful authentication from unusual source or after failures.

techniques.name: Valid Accounts: Domain Accounts
techniques.description: Domain accounts used to persist and move laterally.
techniques.detection_hint: Domain account logon from unexpected host.

techniques.name: Valid Accounts: Local Accounts
techniques.description: Local accounts used for persistence.
techniques.detection_hint: New or rarely used local account authentication.

techniques.name: Brute Force
techniques.description: Adversary may use brute force techniques to gain access to accounts.
techniques.detection_hint: Repeated failed authentication from a single source.

techniques.name: Brute Force: Password Guessing
techniques.description: Guessing of account passwords without further manipulation.
techniques.detection_hint: Threshold of failed logins per source/account pair.

techniques.name: Brute Force: Password Spraying
techniques.description: Trying one or a few passwords across many accounts.
techniques.detection_hint: One source failing against many accounts.

techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
techniques.description: Adversary may abuse command and script interpreters to execute commands.
techniques.detection_hint: Script interpreter launched with suspicious arguments.

techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell
techniques.description: PowerShell provides rich access to Windows APIs and is a common execution vector.
techniques.detection_hint: powershell.exe spawned by Office or launched with encoded/bypass flags.

techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Windows Command Shell
techniques.description: cmd.exe execution for command chaining.
techniques.detection_hint: cmd.exe spawned by unusual parents.

techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Windows Script Host
techniques.description: wscript/cscript execution of .vbs/.js payloads.
techniques.detection_hint: wscript.exe or cscript.exe executing files from user directories.

techniques.name: Windows Management Instrumentation
techniques.description: WMI used to execute remote and local commands.
techniques.detection_hint: wmic.exe process creation or remote WMI execution events.

techniques.name: User Execution
techniques.description: An adversary may rely upon a user opening a malicious file to gain execution.
techniques.detection_hint: User-launched executable or macro-enabled document.

techniques.name: User Execution: Malicious File
techniques.description: User opened a malicious attachment or downloaded file.
techniques.detection_hint: File written then immediately executed by the same user.

techniques.name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution
techniques.description: Adversary may configure components to execute at system startup.
techniques.detection_hint: Registry Run key or startup folder modification.

techniques.name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
techniques.description: Persistence via Run/RunOnce keys or the Startup folder.
techniques.detection_hint: Write to HKCU/HKLM ...\Run or the user Startup folder.

techniques.name: Create or Modify System Process
techniques.description: Adversary may create or modify system-level processes.
techniques.detection_hint: New Windows service registration.

techniques.name: Create or Modify System Process: Windows Service
techniques.description: Persistence or privilege escalation via Windows services.
techniques.detection_hint: Service creation with binary in writable path.

techniques.name: Scheduled Task/Job
techniques.description: Adversary may schedule tasks for execution.
techniques.detection_hint: schtasks.exe or TaskScheduler events.

techniques.name: Scheduled Task/Job: Scheduled Task
techniques.description: Windows scheduled task creation.
techniques.detection_hint: Task registration via schtasks or XML task file write.

techniques.name: Create Account
techniques.description: Adversary may create an account to maintain access.
techniques.detection_hint: net user / add-localgroupmember events.

techniques.name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism
techniques.description: Adversary may bypass mechanisms that constrain privilege elevation.
techniques.detection_hint: UAC bypass binaries or elevation prompts.

techniques.name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Bypass User Account Control
techniques.description: Bypassing UAC to execute with elevated privileges.
techniques.detection_hint: fodhelper/eventvwr/sdclt launched with auto-elevation patterns.

techniques.name: Access Token Manipulation
techniques.description: Adversary may modify access tokens to run under another user's context.
techniques.detection_hint: Token impersonation or duplicate/adjust token APIs.

techniques.name: Obfuscated Files or Information
techniques.description: Adversary may obfuscate files or commands to evade detection.
techniques.detection_hint: Encoded PowerShell or base64 blobs in command lines.

techniques.name: System Binary Proxy Execution
techniques.description: Adversary may bypass controls by proxying execution through trusted binaries.
techniques.detection_hint: rundll32/regsvr32/mshta invoked with unusual arguments.

techniques.name: System Binary Proxy Execution: rundll32
techniques.description: rundll32.exe used to execute DLLs or JavaScript.
techniques.detection_hint: rundll32 with javascript:/http arguments.

techniques.name: Modify Registry
techniques.description: Adversary may modify the registry to hide artifacts or aid execution.
techniques.detection_hint: High-volume registry writes by unusual processes.

techniques.name: Indicator Removal
techniques.description: Adversary may delete or modify artifacts to evade detection.
techniques.detection_hint: Log clearing or timestomping activity.

techniques.name: OS Credential Dumping
techniques.description: Adversary may dump operating system credentials.
techniques.detection_hint: LSASS access or credential dumper tooling.

techniques.name: OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory
techniques.description: Dumping LSASS to extract credential material.
techniques.detection_hint: Process access to lsass.exe or mimikatz-like tool names.

techniques.name: Credentials from Password Stores
techniques.description: Adversary may search for credentials in password managers/browsers.
techniques.detection_hint: Access to browser or credential store files.

techniques.name: Unsecured Credentials
techniques.description: Credentials stored in files or scripts.
techniques.detection_hint: Reading of configuration files containing secrets.

techniques.name: Network Service Discovery
techniques.description: Adversary may attempt to discover systems and services on a network.
techniques.detection_hint: Many destination ports or hosts contacted in a short time.

techniques.name: Remote System Discovery
techniques.description: Adversary may try to identify remote systems.
techniques.detection_hint: net view/adsi enumeration or scanning traffic.

techniques.name: Account Discovery
techniques.description: Adversary may attempt to enumerate accounts.
techniques.detection_hint: net user / Get-LocalUser enumeration commands.

techniques.name: Remote Services
techniques.description: Adversary may use valid accounts to log into remote services.
techniques.detection_hint: SMB/WinRM/RDP logons to internal hosts.

techniques.name: Remote Services: SMB/Windows Admin Shares
techniques.description: PsExec-style execution over SMB admin shares.
techniques.detection_hint: PSEXESVC service creation and ADMIN$ share writes.

techniques.name: Remote Services: Windows Remote Management
techniques.description: WinRM used for remote execution.
techniques.detection_hint: WinRM sessions or port 5985/5986 connections.

techniques.name: Lateral Tool Transfer
techniques.description: Adversary may transfer tools to remote systems.
techniques.detection_hint: File copy to ADMIN$ or remote share.

techniques.name: Application Layer Protocol
techniques.description: Adversary may use application layer protocols for C2.
techniques.detection_hint: Regular outbound connections to external hosts.

techniques.name: Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
techniques.description: C2 over HTTP/HTTPS.
techniques.detection_hint: Script processes initiating external HTTP/S connections.

techniques.name: Application Layer Protocol: DNS
techniques.description: C2 or exfiltration over DNS.
techniques.detection_hint: Long or high-entropy DNS queries.

techniques.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
techniques.description: Adversary may transfer tools or files into the environment.
techniques.detection_hint: Download utilities writing executables to disk.

techniques.name: Dynamic Resolution
techniques.description: Adversary may dynamically resolve C2 infrastructure.
techniques.detection_hint: DGA-like domains or fast-flux DNS.

techniques.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
techniques.description: Data may be exfiltrated over an existing C2 channel.
techniques.detection_hint: Large outbound transfers to a C2 endpoint.

techniques.name: Archive Collected Data
techniques.description: Adversary may archive data prior to exfiltration.
techniques.detection_hint: Archive utilities (tar/7z/zip) with broad paths.

techniques.name: Data from Local System
techniques.description: Adversary may search local system for files of interest.
techniques.detection_hint: Bulk reads of documents or database files.

INITIAL ACCESS.reason: Execution activity without a visible delivery vector suggests an initial-access step was missed (phishing or drive-by).

EXECUTION.reason: A payload executed after a file/download step usually implies user execution of the file.

PERSISTENCE.reason: Post-exploitation chains commonly add an autostart entry that was not observed.

CREDENTIAL ACCESS.reason: Lateral movement or privilege escalation is frequently preceded by credential dumping.

DISCOVERY.reason: Attackers usually enumerate services before moving laterally.

LATERAL MOVEMENT.reason: Movement between hosts typically uses remote services such as SMB admin shares.

COMMAND AND CONTROL.reason: Downloaded payloads usually establish a C2 channel that was not captured.

DEFENSE EVASION.reason: Obfuscation steps between execution stages are common but often invisible in telemetry.

PRIVILEGE ESCALATION.reason: Post-access activity frequently includes an elevation step.

COLLECTION.reason: Data staged for exfiltration is often collected silently.

EXFILTRATION.reason: An established C2 channel may have carried exfiltration that was not logged.

IMPACT.reason: Destructive outcomes may occur outside logged telemetry.
